paragraphs: Studying political language over time requires records that cover many years and retain information about the speeches they contain. Such resources are scarce for Greek. This paper introduces a curated collection of Greek parliamentary proceedings spanning 1989–2020, containing more than one million speeches extracted from 5,355 parliamentary sitting records.

The contribution includes extensive metadata alongside the speech texts, as well as an account of how the collection was constructed and the challenges encountered. Bringing these records into a curated dataset makes it possible to connect computational analysis of language with questions about political discourse across a substantial historical period.

The authors demonstrate this connection by studying changes in word usage over time, across political parties, and around significant historical events. They evaluate and apply algorithms that detect semantic shifts: changes in how words are used or what they mean. The resulting resource supports both linguistic and political analysis, with the demonstration showing how those two purposes can be combined.
neurips-2022-a-greek-parliament-proceedi.tldr: A curated collection of over one million Greek parliamentary speeches supports research into political discourse and changes in word usage.

paragraphs: In a dueling bandit problem, a learner compares pairs of options and receives feedback about which one wins. Updating the learning strategy after every comparison can be impractical in large ranking or recommendation systems. This paper asks whether comparisons can be organized into batches while retaining nearly the performance of fully sequential learning.

The answer depends on the Condorcet condition: there is an option that beats every other option in pairwise preference probability. Under this condition, the proposed algorithm uses O(log(T)) adaptive rounds over a time horizon T. Its asymptotic regret bound is O(K² log²(K)) + O(K log(T)), where K is the number of options and regret measures the cost of imperfect choices.

These bounds nearly match the best known sequential bounds under the same condition, despite requiring far fewer opportunities to update the strategy. Experiments on several real-world datasets also show almost the same performance as algorithms that update in all T rounds. The contribution therefore combines a conditional theoretical guarantee with empirical evidence that batching need not substantially compromise learning performance.
neurips-2022-an-asymptotically-optimal-b.tldr: Under the Condorcet condition, a batched comparison algorithm nearly matches sequential regret bounds using only logarithmically many adaptive rounds.

paragraphs: Parametric CAD sketches contain recurring design patterns that help designers build modular and regular structures. Designers often use these patterns without explicitly defining them as reusable concepts. This paper develops a learning approach that discovers such concepts directly from raw sketches, turning repeated structure in existing designs into something a model can recognize and generate.

The method represents concept structure in two complementary ways. An implicit representation supports detecting concepts in sketches, while an explicit representation supports generating them. It also separates the generation of a concept's structure from the assignment of its parameters. This distinction lets the learned concept describe a reusable pattern whose particular parameter values can vary.

These components are learned together through end-to-end training. The authors demonstrate concept learning on a large CAD sketch dataset and show applications to interpreting design intent and automatically completing sketches. The significance is that the learned units concern recurring modular structure, providing a way to connect sketch recognition with the generation of parameterized design elements.
neurips-2022-discovering-design-concepts.tldr: The method learns recurring modular concepts from CAD sketches and uses them to interpret design intent and complete sketches.

paragraphs: Nearest-neighbor classification predicts a sample's class from similar training examples. With only a few examples, uncertainty in their features can make those similarities unreliable. This paper formulates weighted nearest-neighbor learning as a minimax problem: choose a classifier that performs well against the least favorable feature distributions within a specified uncertainty set.

The proposed algorithm, Dr.k-NN, efficiently solves this optimization problem and assigns minimax-optimal weights to training samples. Those weights depend on the class being considered and on feature similarities under unfavorable scenarios. Consequently, the contribution of a training example reflects the robustness objective, making uncertainty part of how the classifier combines nearby evidence.

When the uncertainty set is properly tuned, the resulting classifier has a smaller Lipschitz norm than ordinary k-NN, meaning its predictions vary less sharply with changes in the input. The authors connect this property to improved generalization. They also combine the method with neural feature embeddings and report competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods in real-data experiments with few training samples.
neurips-2022-distributionally-robust-wei.tldr: Dr.k-NN learns class-dependent neighbor weights that hedge against feature uncertainty and performs competitively when training data are scarce.

paragraphs: A model can perform unevenly across demographic groups when its training data poorly represent the people it later encounters. This connects algorithmic fairness with distribution shift, the problem of learning under one data distribution and making predictions under another. The paper examines how methods developed for these two concerns can help each other.

In one direction, the authors show that enforcing suitable notions of individual fairness can improve accuracy outside the training distribution. This result is established under the covariate shift assumption, where the input distribution changes while the relationship between inputs and outcomes remains the same. The claim concerns appropriate fairness notions under that assumption, rather than every fairness intervention under every shift.

In the other direction, the authors show that representation alignment methods from domain adaptation can be adapted to enforce individual fairness. This creates a connection between methods for making representations work across distributions and methods for treating individuals fairly. The contribution is a two-way methodological relationship: fairness interventions can support adaptation, and adaptation techniques can support fairness.
neurips-2022-domain-adaptation-meets-ind.tldr: Suitable individual-fairness interventions can improve accuracy under covariate shift, while domain-adaptation methods can be adapted to enforce individual fairness.

paragraphs: Image-editing models often regenerate an entire image even when a user changes only a small region. This paper introduces Spatially Sparse Inference, which takes advantage of gradual edits by caching the original image's feature maps. It applies convolutional computation to edited regions and reuses cached features for regions that remain unchanged.

The approach applies to both conditional GANs and diffusion models. The authors also develop the Sparse Incremental Generative Engine, or SIGE, to turn reduced computation into lower execution time on standard hardware. This distinction matters because performing fewer mathematical operations and delivering a faster interactive edit are related but separate achievements.

For edits covering 1.2% of the image, the method reduces DDIM computation by 7.5 times and GauGAN computation by 18 times while preserving visual fidelity. With SIGE, DDIM runs 3.0 times faster on an RTX 3090 and 6.6 times faster on an Apple M1 Pro CPU; GauGAN gains are 4.2 and 14 times, respectively. These results demonstrate substantial benefits for the reported small-edit setting.
neurips-2022-efficient-spatially-sparse-.tldr: Reusing cached features outside edited image regions substantially reduces computation and inference time for conditional GANs and diffusion models.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization links an outer optimization problem to the solution of an inner one, as happens in hyperparameter selection and meta learning. This paper addresses problems with a nonconvex, potentially nonsmooth outer objective and a strongly convex inner objective. Its goal is to reduce computational cost while allowing nonsmooth regularization that earlier methods do not accommodate.

The authors introduce BiO-BreD for deterministic problems, using Bregman distance to guide optimization updates. They also develop SBiO-BreD for stochastic problems, where gradients are approximated from randomness in the problem or data. An accelerated version, ASBiO-BreD, incorporates variance reduction to improve the efficiency of these stochastic updates.

The deterministic method improves on the best known computational complexity cited by the authors. The accelerated stochastic method improves complexity dependence on the condition number and target accuracy when finding an approximately stationary point. This is a stationarity result for the nonconvex outer problem. Experiments on data hyper-cleaning and hyper-representation learning also show the proposed algorithms outperforming related bilevel approaches.
neurips-2022-enhanced-bilevel-optimizati.tldr: Bregman-distance methods improve computational bounds for bilevel problems with strongly convex inner objectives and potentially nonsmooth, nonconvex outer objectives.

paragraphs: Single-cell RNA sequencing produces count data, often with many small values. Graphical models designed for continuous measurements can therefore be inappropriate for inferring networks from these observations. This paper uses a Poisson log-normal model, where the network is represented by the precision matrix of an underlying normal distribution associated with the observed counts.

The proposed estimator, PLNet, works in two stages. It first estimates the latent covariance matrix through maximum marginal likelihood. It then estimates the precision matrix using a lasso-penalized D-trace loss. Separating these stages provides a route from count observations to an estimate of the matrix that encodes the model's network relationships.

The authors establish convergence rates for both stages and sign consistency for the precision estimator in high dimensions. They also show consistency even when model dimension grows exponentially with sample size, despite the Poisson log-normal model lacking sub-Gaussian behavior. Simulations and analyses of real single-cell gene regulatory networks evaluate PLNet against available methods, connecting the statistical theory to its intended count-data application.
neurips-2022-estimating-graphical-models.tldr: PLNet estimates networks from count data through a two-stage Poisson log-normal approach with high-dimensional consistency guarantees.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can require many interactions before an agent learns an effective policy, making it expensive for robotics and scientific control tasks. Common exploration strategies inject randomness into reward-seeking behavior or collect information about the environment's dynamics. The latter can spend effort learning details without considering how they relate to the task.

This paper proposes planning exploration around uncertainty about the optimal trajectory: the sequence of states and actions that would best accomplish the task. The method selects an action sequence to maximize expected information gain about that trajectory. Its choices therefore depend both on the task being pursued and on what the agent currently knows about the environment's dynamics.

Across diverse low-to-medium dimensional control tasks, the authors report learning strong policies with two times fewer samples than strong exploration baselines and 200 times fewer than model-free methods. The evaluation covers both open-loop and closed-loop control. These findings support the value of targeting exploration toward information about successful task execution in the settings studied.
neurips-2022-exploration-via-planning-fo.tldr: Planning actions to learn about the task's optimal trajectory reduces the interactions needed to learn strong policies in tested control tasks.

paragraphs: Robust regression seeks useful fits even when some observations are outliers. This paper develops variants of iteratively reweighted least squares, or IRLS, for nonsmooth regression objectives based on ℓp measures with p between zero and one. IRLS approaches the difficult objective through repeated weighted least-squares problems, updating how strongly observations influence the fit.

For the convex case p = 1, the authors prove global linear convergence under a deterministic feature-matrix condition called the stable range space property. For nonconvex values between zero and one, a similar condition gives local convergence to the global minimizer at superlinear order 2 − p. The rate approaches quadratic as p approaches zero, but this guarantee is local.

Applications include real phase retrieval, regression without correspondences, and robust face restoration. The reported results show greater tolerance of outliers than other methods, faster execution at equal accuracy, and satisfactory restoration of a sparsely corrupted face image. The paper thus combines explicit convergence conditions with practical evidence for solving robust regression problems efficiently.
neurips-2022-global-linear-and-local-sup.tldr: New IRLS variants provide conditional global linear or local superlinear convergence guarantees and strong empirical results for robust regression.

paragraphs: Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles, or PATE, combines predictions from multiple teacher models through noisy voting. The added noise provides a differential privacy guarantee concerning the teachers' training data. This paper identifies a different privacy concern: the randomness of the resulting predictions can reveal information about how the teachers voted on a particular input.

The authors describe an adversary that exploits this stochastic behavior to reconstruct high-fidelity vote histograms. Those histograms reveal the distribution of teacher votes and can expose sensitive attributes of the input, including race, gender, or age. The reported attack relies on the noise added for differential privacy and would not be possible without that noise.

Counterintuitively, the attack becomes easier as more noise is added to strengthen differential privacy. This does not directly break the stated differential privacy guarantee, because the leakage concerns a different privacy expectation. The result shows why a formal guarantee about training data does not by itself resolve every sensitive-information risk associated with a learning system's outputs.
neurips-2022-in-differential-privacy-the.tldr: Noise in PATE can enable recovery of teacher vote histograms and sensitive input attributes without directly violating its differential privacy guarantee.

paragraphs: An incentive designer tries to guide self-interested agents toward a desirable outcome by changing their payoffs. This creates a bilevel problem: the designer chooses incentives while anticipating the equilibrium reached by agents playing a noncooperative game. Repeatedly solving that equilibrium can be expensive, yet skipping it can lead to a suboptimal incentive design.

The paper proposes a single-loop method in which the designer and the agents each take just one step per iteration. While the agents adjust their behavior, the designer gradually learns how incentives influence their overall response. This allows incentive updates and game play to proceed together without repeatedly completing an equilibrium calculation before the next design step.

The authors establish convergence rates for a broad class of games and show that learning the overall incentive influence guarantees optimality after convergence. The contribution addresses the computational dilemma directly: coordinated incremental updates can retain an optimality guarantee within the analyzed setting. Its significance lies in coupling the learning processes of the designer and the agents.
neurips-2022-inducing-equilibria-via-inc.tldr: A single-loop incentive-design method updates designers and agents together while retaining optimality after convergence for the analyzed game setting.

paragraphs: Data centers may use several load balancers to distribute work across heterogeneous processing resources. Each balancer sees only part of a changing system, complicating coordinated decisions. Although centralized training can help multi-agent reinforcement learning, it adds communication and management overhead in networking systems that favor distributed components and straightforward deployment.

This paper models load balancing as a Markov potential game. Its potential function is a carefully designed measure of fairness in workload distribution, linking the agents' decisions to a shared system-level quantity. The authors then propose a fully distributed multi-agent learning algorithm that approximates a Nash equilibrium of this game, where individual agents have little incentive to change their policies unilaterally.

Evaluation uses both an event-driven simulator and a real system. The method achieves close-to-optimal performance in simulation and outperforms production load balancers in the real-system tests. Here, fairness refers to how workloads are distributed. The results suggest that this game-based formulation can support effective coordination while accommodating the distributed operation of the network.
neurips-2022-learning-distributed-and-fa.tldr: A fully distributed reinforcement-learning method uses workload fairness to coordinate load balancers and performs strongly in simulations and a real system.

paragraphs: Convolutional kernels have improved image classification, but explaining precisely why their architectural choices help remains difficult. This paper studies how convolution, pooling, and downsampling affect both the functions a kernel can represent and the data needed to learn them. It focuses on a single layer in a stylized setting with pixels uniformly distributed on a hypercube.

The authors exactly characterize the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space, or RKHS: the function space defined by the kernel. They then use that characterization to calculate sharp high-dimensional asymptotics for generalization error for any given target function. This connects the structure imposed by the architecture to both representational ability and prediction error.

The analysis quantifies sample-complexity gains from convolution's locality and from the approximate translation invariance introduced by average pooling. It also describes the tradeoff between approximation and generalization: an architectural constraint changes what can be represented while influencing how efficiently it can be learned. These are precise theoretical results for the specified one-layer, hypercube setting.
neurips-2022-learning-with-convolution-a.tldr: An exact analysis of one-layer convolutional kernels quantifies how locality and pooling trade representational flexibility for improved sample efficiency.

paragraphs: Generating an object with several desired properties is difficult when those properties are correlated. Changing one property can partly change others, and multiple requested properties may conflict. This paper addresses that joint-control problem with a deep generative framework designed to recover both the meaning of properties and the relationships among them.

The framework uses disentangled latent vectors to represent properties and an explainable mask pooling layer to handle their correlations. It also connects the latent vectors and properties through mutual dependence so that generated objects retain the properties of interest. These components make the relationships between requested attributes part of the generation process.

A multi-objective optimization framework manages simultaneous property requirements, including their correlations and conflicts. The experiments report superior performance in producing objects with desired properties. The central contribution is a mechanism for coordinated control: the generator accounts for how property requests interact, helping it preserve requested characteristics while handling dependencies that make separate control of each property difficult.
neurips-2022-multi-objective-deep-data-g.tldr: A generative framework models correlations between properties to better produce objects satisfying multiple interacting requirements.

paragraphs: Matching 3D shapes means finding which points correspond across different objects or deformations. Neural Correspondence Prior, or NCP, builds on the observation that some 3D network architectures produce plausible matching features even before training. The authors also observe that training a feature extractor on noisy matches tends to remove artifacts from those matches.

The method turns these observations into a two-stage process. First, an adapted unsupervised approach produces an initial set of noisy correspondences. Second, those correspondences become supervision for training another network. Although the second stage uses a supervised training procedure, the overall approach remains unsupervised because the matching labels are generated by the method itself.

The authors report significant accuracy improvements, especially when training over a collection of shapes. NCP can also produce high-quality matches in challenging settings such as sparse point clouds and non-isometric meshes, where existing methods fail. Reported results describe the approach as fast, data-efficient, and state of the art on many tasks, supporting the use of neural feature learning as a correspondence-denoising mechanism.
neurips-2022-ncp-neural-correspondence-p.tldr: NCP improves unsupervised 3D shape matching by training networks on automatically generated noisy correspondences that the networks tend to denoise.

paragraphs: Online learning requires decisions to be made as new challenges arrive. This paper introduces a framework in which a learner faces an adversary in a game that changes each round and produces multiple outcome values. The learner's objective lacks the convex-concave structure needed for the usual minimax theorem, making standard reasoning about the game unavailable.

Despite that difficulty, the authors provide a simple algorithm that competes with a benchmark where the adversary must reveal its action first. Its regret diminishes at an optimal rate. This gives a common way to analyze multiple objectives in changing adversarial games, even though the learner does not receive the advance information available in the benchmark.

The framework recovers optimal bounds and efficient algorithms for multicalibration, several no-regret learning settings, and a polytope version of Blackwell approachability with fast convergence. It also yields a new method for competing with collections of forecasters through multicalibeating. For that application, the dependence on the number of competing models improves exponentially over prior work.
neurips-2022-online-minimax-multiobjecti.tldr: A general online multiobjective framework achieves optimal diminishing regret and improves dependence on ensemble size for multicalibeating forecasters.

paragraphs: Coupling flows are invertible neural networks whose usefulness depends on which transformations they can represent. This paper studies their ability to approximate diffeomorphisms, smooth invertible maps with smooth inverses. It considers approximation in the C^k norm, which controls derivatives through order k as well as the values of the transformation itself.

The authors prove universality when the layers can approximate certain transformations that change a single coordinate. They further show that compositions of affine coupling layers and invertible linear transformations achieve this universality. The results are extended to transformations that depend on additional parameters, producing approximation theorems for the parametric architecture called Para-CFlows.

Derivative-aware approximation matters for the paper's application: using a neural model as a surrogate in contextual Bayesian optimization. The authors apply Para-CFlows to these tasks and report better optimization performance and gradient approximations than other neural surrogates. The theoretical contribution establishes expressive capacity under the stated layer condition, while the experiments demonstrate practical advantages in the evaluated optimization tasks.
neurips-2022-para-cflows-c-k-universal-d.tldr: Para-CFlows extend derivative-aware universality results for invertible networks to parametric maps and improve tested Bayesian-optimization surrogate performance.

paragraphs: Facility location asks how to choose a shared facility's position from agents' reported locations. This paper introduces Strong Proportionality, a fairness requirement that gives two groups at different locations equal total cost. The authors show that no deterministic mechanism can satisfy this requirement while also being strategyproof, meaning agents cannot benefit by misreporting their locations.

Randomization changes what is possible. The proposed Random Rank mechanism uniformly chooses a rank from one through the number of agents and places the facility at that ranked agent location. It satisfies Strong Proportionality in expectation. The main theorem establishes that it is the unique randomized mechanism combining universal truthfulness, universal anonymity, and this expected fairness property.

The paper also studies AverageOrRandomRank, which achieves stronger fairness guarantees for realized outcomes by weakening the incentive requirement to strategyproofness in expectation. This distinguishes guarantees that hold across individual realizations from those that hold after averaging over randomness. The contribution identifies both a uniquely characterized mechanism and a tradeoff between the strength of incentive and fairness guarantees.
neurips-2022-random-rank-the-one-and-onl.tldr: Random Rank uniquely combines universal truthfulness, universal anonymity, and Strong Proportionality in expectation for randomized facility location.

paragraphs: Two classifiers can have statistically indistinguishable overall performance while giving conflicting predictions for the same person. This predictive multiplicity can make consequential decisions depend on an otherwise unjustified choice between models. The paper introduces Rashomon Capacity to measure this ambiguity for probabilistic classifiers, whose outputs include scores rather than only yes-or-no labels.

Earlier multiplicity measures focus on thresholded class predictions. Rashomon Capacity captures finer differences in the probabilities assigned to individual samples, allowing disagreement to be measured beyond whether two models cross the same decision threshold. The authors provide a rigorous derivation of the metric, explain its interpretation, and show how it can be estimated in practice.

The metric also supports principled ways to disclose conflicting models to stakeholders. Numerical experiments across datasets and learning models, including neural networks, illustrate the kinds of predictive variation it captures. The intended use is to help data scientists measure and report model-dependent uncertainty before deployment, making disagreements visible even when aggregate performance offers little basis for choosing among classifiers.
neurips-2022-rashomon-capacity-a-metric-.tldr: Rashomon Capacity measures how similarly performing probabilistic classifiers disagree on individual predictions and supports reporting those conflicts.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning research often trains agents from scratch, even though developing large systems involves repeated changes to their design and algorithms. Discarding previous training makes those iterations expensive. This paper proposes reincarnating reinforcement learning as a workflow in which learned policies and other prior computational work are reused across agent versions or transferred between agents.

The authors investigate a specific step toward that broader goal: efficiently transferring an existing, suboptimal policy into a standalone value-based agent. They find that existing approaches fail in this setting and propose a simple algorithm to address their limitations. The focus is therefore on making prior learning useful even when the available policy is imperfect.

Experiments demonstrate gains over learning from scratch on Atari 2600 games, a challenging locomotion task, and real-world stratospheric-balloon navigation. These results support reuse as a practical development strategy across the tested settings. The wider argument is that preserving prior computation could reduce the resources needed for reinforcement-learning research and make real-world adoption more accessible.
neurips-2022-reincarnating-reinforcement.tldr: Reincarnating reinforcement learning reuses earlier policies to accelerate new agents, with demonstrated gains across games, locomotion, and balloon navigation.

paragraphs: Deep networks can rely on shortcuts: decision rules that succeed on ordinary benchmarks but fail under more challenging testing conditions. Once a shortcut works, the model may have little reason to learn other useful features. This paper introduces a training framework that temporarily makes existing knowledge insufficient, encouraging the network to acquire additional task-related information.

The framework creates a gently modified task and places a roadblock on the shortcuts the model has learned. Because those shortcuts no longer suffice to complete the modified task, training pushes the network to develop other features. The intervention targets the learning process by changing what knowledge is needed for successful performance.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets report significant improvements in classification accuracy and feature diversity. Visualizations also support the authors' proposed explanation of how the method works. These findings indicate that temporarily obstructing shortcut-based solutions can reduce over-reliance on them and encourage more robust features, with the evidence covering both predictive performance and the diversity of learned information.
neurips-2022-roadblocks-for-temporarily-.tldr: Temporarily modifying tasks so learned shortcuts are insufficient improves classification accuracy and encourages more diverse, robust features.

paragraphs: A Markov decision process describes how actions lead probabilistically to future states. Estimating those probabilities from limited data introduces uncertainty that can undermine planning. This paper learns uncertain MDPs, which represent possible transition probabilities through uncertainty sets and support policies evaluated against the worst-case model within those sets.

The approach combines a dedicated Bayesian inference scheme with robust policy computation. It represents transition probabilities as intervals and updates them as observations arrive, including when new data conflict with the current intermediate model. Learning can be stopped at any point to compute a robust policy from an uncertain MDP that reflects the data collected so far.

This anytime capability allows policy computation without waiting for a fixed learning process to finish, and the method can adapt to environmental changes. Robust specifications, such as safety constraints, are assessed relative to the modeled uncertainty set. Benchmark experiments demonstrate effectiveness and compare the approach with robust policies based on uncertain MDPs learned using the UCRL2 reinforcement-learning algorithm.
neurips-2022-robust-anytime-learning-of-.tldr: An anytime Bayesian method learns uncertain transition models that support robust policy computation and adapt to conflicting data or environmental changes.

paragraphs: Object-centric video learning aims to represent a scene as distinct entities that can be segmented and tracked. Earlier slot-based approaches using motion cues struggle with complex real-world videos. SAVi++ explores whether depth information can supply the geometric signal needed to learn object structure in scenes containing more varied appearances, backgrounds, and camera movement.

The model learns a slot-based video representation by predicting depth signals. Combined with practices for scaling the model, this training enables segmentation of dynamic scenes recorded by moving cameras, including both stationary and moving objects. The approach does not require segmentation supervision, though depth prediction supplies a training signal about the structure of the scene.

The authors also demonstrate learning from sparse LiDAR depth measurements in the real-world Waymo Open dataset. Object segmentation and tracking emerge from this training setup. The result supports the hypothesis that scene geometry can help organize video representations around objects, extending object-centric learning toward complex conditions where motion-based slot models had struggled.
neurips-2022-savi-towards-end-to-end-obj.tldr: SAVi++ learns to segment and track objects in complex videos by predicting depth from slot-based representations without segmentation supervision.

paragraphs: Kronecker regression is a least-squares problem whose design matrix is built as a Kronecker product of smaller factor matrices. This structure appears repeatedly when alternating least squares computes a Tucker tensor decomposition. Faster regression routines can therefore reduce the cost of recurring steps in an important method for representing multidimensional data.

The authors present the first subquadratic-time algorithm for a multiplicative 1 + ε approximation that avoids a running-time term proportional to ε raised to minus the number of factors. The approach combines leverage-score sampling with iterative methods. Removing that particular exponential dependence addresses a computational obstacle as the number of factor matrices increases.

The method also extends to block-structured design matrices containing a Kronecker-product block. This yields subquadratic algorithms for Kronecker ridge regression and Tucker factor-matrix updates, which are not themselves pure Kronecker regression problems. Together, these extensions improve the running time of every Tucker ALS step. Experiments on synthetic data and real image tensors demonstrate the regression algorithm's speed and accuracy.
neurips-2022-subquadratic-kronecker-regr.tldr: A sampling-and-iteration algorithm accelerates approximate Kronecker regression and all Tucker ALS steps while avoiding an exponential accuracy-dependent runtime term.
